title: Slope
status: draft: written by Claude, waiting for owner review

hints.lin.slope.points: Slope = change in y ÷ change in x. Subtract the y's and the x's in the same order.
hints.lin.slope.graph: Pick two points on the line. Count the run across and the rise up (down is negative). Slope = rise ÷ run.
hints.lin.slope: Slope = rise ÷ run = change in y ÷ change in x. Same order for both; simplify.

misconceptionMessages.lin.slope-run-over-rise: It's rise over run: the change in y goes on top, the change in x on the bottom.
misconceptionMessages.lin.slope-mixed-order: Subtract in the same order both times: (y₂ − y₁) and (x₂ − x₁). A line going down from left to right has a negative slope.
misconceptionMessages.lin.slope-rise-only: That's the rise. Divide it by the run (the change in x) to get the slope.

sections.title: Slope from two points
sections.objective: Find the slope between two points, or from a table.
explain: Slope measures how steep a line is: how much y changes for each 1 that x changes.
Subtract the y's, subtract the x's in the same order, divide, and simplify.
sections.key: Slope = change in y ÷ change in x. Subtract in the same order both times.

sections.title: Slope from a graph
sections.objective: Count rise and run on a graph.
explain: Pick two points where the line crosses the grid exactly.
Count across (run), then up or down (rise). Down is negative.

visual.caption: Tap to draw the run, then the rise.

sections.key: Count the run across and the rise up (down is negative) between two points on the line. Slope = rise ÷ run.

sections.title: Putting it together
sections.objective: Slope from points, tables and graphs, mixed.
